newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia 1997 consumer prices seen up 3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia 1997 consumer prices seen up 3.5 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's consumer price index (CPI) is expected to rise by 3.5 percent in 1997 after an estimated 3.6 percent gain in 1996, the Ministry of Finance said on Friday in its 1996/97 Economic Report.
In 1995, the CPI rose by 3.4 percent.

The government said a combination of policy measures directed at managing demand, expanding supply as well as improving distribution and trading practices helped keep prices stable despite increasing pressures.
Tighter monetary policy, fiscal restraint and the abolition or reduction of import duties helped curb inflationary pressures, the ministry said in its annual report.
The government last year also imposed restrictions on property sales.

Among the components of the CPI, the index for food showed the highest rise of 5.7 percent during the first nine months of 1996, contributing to 57.1 percent of the overall CPI increase in the period.
